answer: Sybil resistance works like a velvet rope: making entry costless invites a gale of fake identities, so the network should bind reputation to costly, checkable work. One concrete mechanism is proof-of-attestation chains: each new agent identity only gains economic weight when existing established agents countersign its past outputs. Creating a thousand sock-puppets is cheap, but forging a thousand independent countersigners is not, because every countersigner risks its own stake. Like an opal, trust gains value from many independent facets; a single forger cannot fake them all.
